body:
To sum up, we're now validating the generated JAXBContext at build time, so users can fix this kind of failure before running the application, but the Quarkus CXF and Camel Quarkus extensions use third-party dependencies that produce an invalid JAXBContext and you can't fix this because you do need these dependencies. 

About the options you suggest:
- A. Validate the JAXB context only if some JAXBContext injection point is available in the user application.

I would not go in this direction because at the moment users want to use the JAXBContext and use one of your extensions, it would fail and users would not directly see how to address it. 

- C. Have some sort of ValidateDefaultJAXBContextBuildItem that would allow third-party...

Again, I would not go in this direction because users would miss this feature if they do want to use the generated JAXBContext. 

Therefore, option B looks good to me. However, I think it would be simpler to create a new build item to exclude the class that causes the conflict. But, on your side, you would need to produce this build time with the mentioned classes. 

Wdyt? @gsmet @ppalaga

> I think it would be simpler to create a new build item to exclude the class that causes the conflict. But, on your side, you would need to produce this build time with the mentioned classes.

I agree, this would be doable, but how can I as a developer of an extension wrapping third party libs know, which classes my users want in their default JAXB context? I frankly do not know which ones I should exclude. I am by no means a JAXB expert. Is there maybe some clear choice here? I'd spontaneously say this should be left up to end users. WDYT?

Yes, end users would need to use the following properties to ensure the generated JAXBContext is ok:
- quarkus.jaxb.validate-jaxb-context=false to disable the validation altogether
- quarkus.jaxb.exclude-classes=a.b.c to exclude the classes that cause the conflict

About how to know it. The JAXB exception should give users this information, so they can address it accordingly. 

I will create a pull request with the new build item.

issue.title: Allow extensions to exclude classes to be found in the JAXB context

body:
I must admit I am not sure how can https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/31651 help me to solve my problem? As I stated above, I have no idea which classes my end users may wish to exclude from the default JAXB context, so I can hardly make any use the new `ExcludeJaxbClassesToBeBoundBuildItem`.

I am trying to implement the option A and it looks quite promissing. Let me send a PR after I add some tests.
And would not a user have the same issue if they inject the jaxbcontext?

I thought in your case, you had identified the conflicts:

this problem is related to the following location:
                at org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.EndpointReferenceType
                at public org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.EndpointReferenceType org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.ObjectFactory.createEndpointReferenceType()
                at org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.ObjectFactory
                at protected java.util.List org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.ReferenceParametersType.any
                at org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.ReferenceParametersType
        this problem is related to the following location:
                at jakarta.xml.ws.wsaddressing.W3CEndpointReference

> And would not a user have the same issue if they inject the jaxbcontext?

By the way, we are considering splitting the extension into two. This is what you mentioned in the option 2. I think it's what have more sense if you dont need a jaxbcontext at all.

Yes, my extensions do not need the default JAXBContext bean to work properly. Splitting would be a valid solution. But still, more modules mean more maintenance so option A. might be better from that point of view.

Still users that want to use the jaxb extension and your extension would see this issue. So excluding for example, the class org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.EndpointReferenceType might still be necessary

> Still users that want to use the jaxb extension and your extension would see this issue. So excluding for example, the class org.apache.cxf.ws.addressing.EndpointReferenceType might still be necessary

Yes, I agree the issue would pop up and I believe it should be the given user's responsibility to choose which of the two classes she wants in the default context. Or she may choose to create her own context instance where she puts only the classes she knows she needs.

Here is my attempt to implement the option A: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/31666 
I think I was able to cover it with tests properly and I prefer it to B.
